### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via packages.disable (sdk, the route ledger binds it to PATCH /packages/:id/disable))_
- `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/disable (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`  _(via /packages/:id/disable (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f54ef61fd48ce4dfbad4925632de2b7c86ab9e9b` — the merge of head `138dbe7f222d07be15597922abcf9594a6d5f855` into base `02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f54ef61fd48ce4dfbad4925632de2b7c86ab9e9b && git checkout f54ef61fd48ce4dfbad4925632de2b7c86ab9e9b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca 138dbe7f222d07be15597922abcf9594a6d5f855 && git checkout -B drift-repro 02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca && git merge --no-ff 138dbe7f222d07be15597922abcf9594a6d5f855

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 02d6507275eaa7d821e98585df9bb31eed8dedca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `138dbe7f222d07be15597922abcf9594a6d5f855`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts (`SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS.disableable` and the block comment), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (`isDisableablePackage`, `withDisableableVerdict`, the two read-door stamps, the disable door's predicate line, the `isDisableableAppModule` header), packages/spec/src/api/package-api.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-disableable-verdict.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-writable-verdict.test.ts (pin 5), packages/runtime/src/domains/package-door-producer-key-carry.test.ts (`DOOR_COMPUTED_STAMPS`), packages/client/src/return-type-precision.test.ts (the two served-row fixtures), content/docs/references/api/package-api-assembled.mdx (regenerated), .changeset/28318-served-disableable-verdict.md

Inputs: card #28318 (body: the Seam from #28117 item 4 with its "⛔ `writable` must not be overloaded"; triage 6539271118: p1 protocol addition, `domain:spec`, one-PR exception for serving it from the runtime; the seat's claim 6539475789), PR #28371 (body with the patched `Skills-docs: follow-up #28118` line, the dev report 6540403697 and its two declared deviations, the file list of 9 files, the diff of 600 lines against `main` read whole, the nine commits from the merge-base b4ccbc6f, and the one commit 138dbe7f over the claimed head b4d79818, read whole: 5 insertions and 4 deletions in `return-type-precision.test.ts`), the 50 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T07:44Z: all 50 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Auto Label, Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test UI (matrix shard/16), UI Published Artifacts), and the tree on `main` for the door this PR re-routes (`packages.ts`: `requireWritablePackage` :572 to :582 answers `null` for a writable package, `isDisableableAppModule` :637 to :647, the disable door :1789 asking `isDisableableAppModule(id) ? null : requireWritablePackage(...)`) and for `withWritableVerdict` :832. The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); none of the files `main` moved since the merge-base is in this diff, and no open PR touches the two source files.

### ① Derived judgments

- **One predicate, served and asked** - right. `isDisableablePackage(engine, id)` is `isDisableableAppModule(engine, id) || isWritablePackage(engine, id)`; the disable door now asks it where it asked `isDisableableAppModule` alone, which is behaviour-identical because the branch it short-circuits, `requireWritablePackage`, already answers `null` for a writable package. `withDisableableVerdict` stamps the same call on `GET /packages` (after the projection, inside the same map as `withWritableVerdict`) and on `GET /packages/:id`, keyed the way `withWritableVerdict` keys the row. The rule is spelled once; the agreement pin (eleven rows, served value against the door's 200 or 422 on a fresh registry) is what holds the two readers together, and the two ablation legs (constant `true`, constant `false`) red the agreement case on every row of the opposite class.
- **The contract** - right. `disableable: z.boolean()` joins `SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS`, so it lands on both stage branches of `InstalledPackageAtEitherStageSchema` and on the list and detail responses; required like `writable`, which both doors already serve on every row; stripped by the record schemas as `writable` is (pinned). The block comment and describe say what the key answers (the package only; the caller's permission and a catalog wall stay at the door) and that neither verdict derives from the other, which is the card's "not overloaded" ruling written into the schema.
- **`writable` and every write door are untouched** - right. A module of an installed app serves `disableable: true`, `writable: false`; `requireWritablePackage` keeps guarding every other verb.
- **The two existing pins edited** - right, and they are the register working: `DOOR_COMPUTED_STAMPS` is a set-equality register of door-computed stamps that must red when a stamp arrives without a decision, and it went red on the first full run until `disableable` was added with its reason; `packages-writable-verdict` pin 5 sets the new key aside by name beside `writable`. Both are tests of `packages.ts`, the surface the order names; declared in the dev report.
- **The client pin follows the served shape** - right. `return-type-precision.test.ts` declares a served row as the record plus the door's verdicts, and `disableable` now sits beside `writable` on both fixtures, which is why `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace` went red on b4d79818 and are green here; it is the ripple of a new served key that the dev report's measurement had not reached, the kind this lane records as a trap. The pin's twelve rows are otherwise unchanged.
- **Reference page and changeset** - right. `package-api-assembled.mdx` is regenerated from the describe (four tables); the changeset names the key, the one predicate, the unchanged `writable` and the reader.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/runtime` minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; `Metadata-protocol: added`** - accepted. A new required key on a served response is a widening of what the server sends (the lane's all-minor precedent for a new served key, #28287); the runtime serves it on two public doors. `Metadata-protocol: added` is right for a new key on the package protocol's served row.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Name approval owed to the maintainer: `disableable`** - the card offered it as an example and triage fixed the lane and the shape (a served boolean beside `writable`) without ruling the spelling; the PR measures the convention (`writable`, `editable`, `deletable`, `resettable`, `undoable`, `repairable`, `sortable`) and the name follows it. Nothing else is owed on the name.
- **`GET /meta/package` stamps `writable` but not `disableable`** - the dev's out-of-scope note: that door's rows are not declared with `SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS`, and the Console's Packages page reads `/packages`, so no consumer misses it today. Serving it there would move the predicate into `metadata-protocol`; a second card if a consumer ever reads that door for Disable.
- **The Console half is #28118** - it offers Disable / Enable from `disableable` and carries the handbook edit (`marketplace-handbook.mdx` "Disabling a module"); `Skills-docs: follow-up #28118` is the right line, and `git grep writable -- skills/` names no package row, so no `skills/**` page is owed.
- **A required key and older servers** - a client that validated a package row against this spec version would refuse a row from a server that predates the key; `@objectstack/client` does not parse these responses through the schema (comments only), and `writable` set the same precedent. Not owed.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Nothing blocking, no should-fix on the diff.** Tried: a row whose `manifest.id` is absent and `id` a string (the fallback mirrors `withWritableVerdict`); `id` undefined (the guard makes `isDisableableAppModule` unreachable and `isWritablePackage` answers as it did for `writable`); a module whose only app dependency is itself (excluded on `main` already); the `?type=module` listing (pinned to serve the same pair). One predicate with two readers, pinned by agreement rather than by restating the rule, is the shape #8146 asks for.

**Verdict reasoning.** The key is declared where `writable` is, with the same requiredness, stripping and placement; the runtime serves it from the one predicate the door asks, and the door's behaviour is provably unchanged; the agreement pin and the two ablations hold the two readers to one answer; the two edited pins are registers doing their job; semver and declarations match; the head is clean against `main` and every check is green or skipped. What remains is the maintainer's word on the name.
